title: Studio and album credits: Joe Turner, Peggy Lee and others
summary: Leeman lists albums he made including Joe Turner Sings the Blues, Billy Butterfield and Bob Crosby albums, Peggy Lee's 'Lover' and a Paul Whiteman album.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: I made an all time record that's considered an all time jazz collector's item with Joe Turner Sings the Blues on Atlantic Records. Now that's a thing that we'll have to get to, and I'll have to explain that because that's a great part of my life, just making it in two days and recording it
with all the stars I had known back in the old days. I was the only white person on those dates, and -- well, we'll get to that later.

I made some recordings that were great sellers, but you know, they were in the commercial vein, too, like being on staff at Decca Records, I recorded "Lover" with Peggy Lee, and I made a Paul Whitman album with Paul in attendance, and we featured Tom and Jimmie Dorsey -- his life -- that's what Whitman was setting up in the album. And I appeared with Bob Crosby's Bobcats at the Rainbow Grill in Manhattan and the Riviera in Las Vegas -- that was my first time in Vegas. That was a beautiful experience. In the late sixties, I was at Condon's, and this is all working -- all these outside things were done while I was working nights, so I could get to play jazz and get that out of my system, and be on call by the contractors. I was just fortunate in being able to do the many exciting dates on the outside that I can't -- hadn't even gotten to and hadn't mentioned yet.
